evidence.claim: The IMF welcomed plans to phase out broad-based energy subsidies, support vulnerable groups, and prioritize productivity-enhancing spending in education, ICT, green-resilient infrastructure, and social protection, while also urging household-debt restructuring.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Thailand
evidence.excerpt: The IMF welcomed plans to phase out broad-based energy subsidies, support vulnerable groups, and prioritize productivity-enhancing spending in education, ICT, green-resilient infrastructure, and social protection, while also urging household-debt restructuring.
evidence.source_locator: key paragraphs on targeted support, fiscal consolidation, and structural reform
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same IMF mission statement, but this passage adds distinct policy guidance on spending quality and debt management.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 policy choices and the near-term policy mix.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to the Prayut government because it describes government policy options and implementation priorities, not a single personal order.
contrary_evidence: The IMF is advising the authorities, so the passage does not prove implementation success by itself.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Thailand's economy recovered to pre-pandemic level in 2022, growth accelerated to 4.5 percent in Q3 on private consumption and tourism, and the government largely maintained proactive fiscal policy to support recovery and cost-of-living relief.
evidence.title: Thailand's economy is projected to recover to its pre-pandemic level in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Thailand's economy recovered to pre-pandemic level in 2022, growth accelerated to 4.5 percent in Q3 on private consumption and tourism, and the government largely maintained proactive fiscal policy to support recovery and cost-of-living relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank Thailand Economic Monitor press release with specific dated findings and policy characterizations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed attribution: part reflects Prayut-era fiscal choices, while the rebound also reflects reopening and tourism normalization.
contrary_evidence: The same release notes the recovery was driven by reopening and global conditions, not just domestic policy.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said 79 percent of Thailand's poor remained in rural areas, poverty reduction slowed from 2015 onward, and 70 percent of rural households reported lower income since March 2020.
evidence.title: Rural Thailand Faces the Largest Poverty Challenges with High Income Inequality
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said 79 percent of Thailand's poor remained in rural areas, poverty reduction slowed from 2015 onward, and 70 percent of rural households reported lower income since March 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank diagnostic summary with direct statistics and a dated launch context.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing the inherited distributional structure affecting 2022 policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited and structural; it limits the degree to which Prayut can be credited for overall welfare outcomes.
contrary_evidence: Because the figures are structural, they do not isolate Prayut-specific policy failure or success in 2022.

evidence.claim: The BOT said ratings downgrades reflected increasing household debt and a fragile tourism-led recovery, while its relief programs had helped borrowers and left the banking system resilient overall.
evidence.title: Bank of Thailand clarifies S&P lowered credit ratings on four Thai commercial banks
evidence.excerpt: The BOT said ratings downgrades reflected increasing household debt and a fragile tourism-led recovery, while its relief programs had helped borrowers and left the banking system resilient overall.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct central-bank release with explicit debt, recovery, and balance-sheet details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Prayut-era policy environment through banking relief and recovery management, but the immediate actor was the central bank.
contrary_evidence: The same release shows a serious debt overhang and fragile recovery, so resilience was incomplete.

evidence.claim: Thailand's parliament passed the first reading of a 3.185 trillion baht budget for fiscal 2023 aimed at supporting recovery, and Prayut said it would restore strong, sustained growth, reduce inequality, and disburse aid transparently.
evidence.title: Parliament passes $93 billion budget bill at first reading
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's parliament passed the first reading of a 3.185 trillion baht budget for fiscal 2023 aimed at supporting recovery, and Prayut said it would restore strong, sustained growth, reduce inequality, and disburse aid transparently.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch with a direct quotation from Prayut and concrete budget figures.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and about the budget that governed the next fiscal year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut because the statement is his and the budget was his government's central fiscal instrument.
contrary_evidence: The passage reports legislative passage, not budget execution or measured outcomes.

evidence.claim: Thailand aimed for 5 million to 15 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2022 after easing travel restrictions, and a meeting chaired by Prayut approved extending domestic-travel support including a 40 percent subsidy on one million room nights.
evidence.title: Thailand targets 5 million to 15 million foreign tourists this year
evidence.excerpt: Thailand aimed for 5 million to 15 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2022 after easing travel restrictions, and a meeting chaired by Prayut approved extending domestic-travel support including a 40 percent subsidy on one million room nights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous report with explicit tourism and support-program details plus chair attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's government through the cabinet/task-force meeting he chaired, though reopening was also a response to the pandemic.
contrary_evidence: Tourism recovery depended heavily on reopening conditions and was still far below 2019 levels.

evidence.claim: Thailand expanded EV incentives, removed some investment barriers, and kept a goal of having 30 percent of total auto output be EVs by 2030.
evidence.title: Thailand approves enhanced incentives to boost EV use
evidence.excerpt: Thailand expanded EV incentives, removed some investment barriers, and kept a goal of having 30 percent of total auto output be EVs by 2030.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a specific policy package with direct quotes from the investment agency.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Prayut government through the BOI and cabinet policy framework, though the BOI led implementation.
contrary_evidence: The article describes an investment-promotion package rather than a proven broad welfare gain.

evidence.claim: Finance Minister Arkhom said stimulus would become more targeted toward vulnerable groups and low-income households as more people returned to work, and that fiscal policy would be more focused.
evidence.title: Thai government spending to target low-income groups - Finance Minister
evidence.excerpt: Finance Minister Arkhom said stimulus would become more targeted toward vulnerable groups and low-income households as more people returned to work, and that fiscal policy would be more focused.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous policy reporting with direct ministerial attribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Prayut government through the finance minister, but the policy statement came from Arkhom rather than Prayut personally.
contrary_evidence: The same report says stimulus was being reduced, so the measure reflects normalization as well as help for the poor.

evidence.claim: Thailand expected overall investment applications to fall 22 percent in 2022 after a first-half slump, with foreign investment more than halving year on year, even though EV and digital projects held up better.
evidence.title: Thailand sees 22% drop in investment pledges this year
evidence.excerpt: Thailand expected overall investment applications to fall 22 percent in 2022 after a first-half slump, with foreign investment more than halving year on year, even though EV and digital projects held up better.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on official BOI data with clear year-on-year figures and sector breakdowns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly attributable to external slowdown rather than Prayut alone, though it still reflects the government's investment climate.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes EV and digital investment remained comparatively strong, so the investment picture was mixed rather than uniformly weak.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice, escalation, or crisis-management episode is shown.
Command-and-control, custody, and safety-governance evidence tied specifically to Prayut remains thin.
PM-level attribution for 2022 international-security choices is still thin; most evidence is ministry or delegation posture.
The Myanmar and Ukraine material does not yet show concrete peace or accountability outcomes attributable to Prayut.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for the APEC crackdown and the deep-south emergency regime remains limited.
The torture/disappearance law is an important reform, but year-end enforcement evidence is still weak.
Direct evidence on the sponsors and mechanism of the election-system change is still thin.
4B.4 and 4B.7 remain under-evidenced relative to the stronger protest, media, and term-limit material.
Budget intent and macro recovery are better evidenced than actual implementation and take-up.
Evidence on appointments, anti-capture, and mistake-correction is still weak.
Direct service-delivery, take-up, and quality evidence is thin outside budget allocations and national surveys.
Ruler-specific causal attribution for rural, child, and mental-health outcomes remains weak.
No independent 2022 finding of personal lying, self-dealing, or concealed conflict of interest is shown.
The package relies too much on allegations, self-defense, and broader regime context.
The program basis is only partly explicit; some objectives are inferred from budgets and coalition moves rather than a single frozen program statement.
Outcome evidence is sectoral and mixed, and external reopening effects remain hard to separate from ruler skill.
